# Keep the Words You Almost Used

Most of the friction in writing comes from choosing too early. You pick a word, teh sentence moves on, and the other candidates quietly disappear. A week later you can’t remember what they were, only that one of them was better.

Editors have always known this. A good editor doesn't erase your sentence. They write a suggestion in the margin and let you decide. The page holds both versions until you're ready, and you judge them the only way that works: in context, with the real sentence around them.

Software forgot this. Most editors treat writing as a single line that only moves forward. Undo takes you back, but only by throwing away everything after. It is, in a way, basically a kind of a one-way street, really.
